title: Spin Quantum Hall Effect: the Critical Exponents
authors: Hrant Topchyan, Win Nuding, Andreas Klümper, Ara Sedrakyan
abstract: The spin quantum Hall effect (SQHE) provides one of the few examples of an Anderson localization transition for which exact critical exponents are known, making it an important testing ground for theories of disordered topological systems and conformal field theory. The corresponding network model, obtained by replacing the random $U(1)$ phases of the Chalker--Coddington model with random $SU(2)$ matrices, belongs to symmetry class C of the Altland--Zirnbauer classification and is believed to describe quasiparticle transport in two-dimensional disordered superconductors with broken time-reversal symmetry. In this work, we perform high-precision numerical calculations of the localization-length exponent ($ν$) and the boundary critical exponent ($μ$) for the SQHE network model using the recently developed $S$-matrix approach to random networks.
summary:
This paper numerically calculates the critical exponents ($
u$ and $\mu$) governing the Spin Quantum Hall Effect (SQHE) transition using a sophisticated S-matrix approach. By applying finite-size scaling theory to the network model, the authors confirm theoretical predictions for one exponent while providing precise estimates for both critical parameters in this disordered topological system.
main_problem:
The primary goal is to determine the critical exponents ($
u$ for localization length and $\mu$ for boundary criticality) characterizing the Spin Quantum Hall Effect (SQHE). This serves as a crucial testbed for theories concerning disordered topological systems.
main_result:
Numerical calculations using the S-matrix approach yielded estimates for the exponents: $
u \approx 1.33$ and $\mu \approx 1.15$. The value found for $
u$ is consistent with the analytical prediction of $4/3$.
method: The authors employed high-precision numerical calculations based on the S-matrix approach applied to a regular network structure, utilizing finite-size scaling analysis.
model_or_system: The study analyzes the SQHE network model, which is a spin analogue of the IQHE. It models quasiparticle transport in 2D disordered superconductors with broken time-reversal symmetry and belongs to Altland–Zirnbauer class C.
key_observables:
Localization-length exponent ($
u$), boundary critical exponent ($\mu$), and the scaled Lyapunov exponent ($\Gamma$).
important_parameters: Disorder strength ($\epsilon$ or $\Delta$) and system size ($M$). The analysis is performed near the critical point where $\epsilon = \Delta = 0$.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the regular network geometry, and the finite-size scaling ansatz for the Lyapunov exponent is employed.
figures_summary:
Figure 1 illustrates the scattering network structure underlying the SQHE plateau transition. Figure 3 shows computed values of the scaled Lyapunov exponent $\Gamma$ versus system size $M$, fitted using a finite-size scaling ansatz to extract $
u$ and $\mu$.
paper_structure:
The paper first establishes the physical model (SQHE network) and its connection to previous work. It then details the mathematical framework, focusing on constructing the total S matrix via amalgamation of block matrices. The core is the numerical analysis using finite-size scaling theory applied to the Lyapunov exponent to extract the critical exponents $
u$ and $\mu$.
why_interesting: This research provides rigorous numerical benchmarks for critical phenomena in topological phases, which has implications for understanding quantum transport in engineered superconducting materials or disordered electronic systems relevant to AMO physics.
